case.case_title: Abasin Banda v. S. I. Gunaratne & Others

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was lawfully arrested according to procedure established by law and informed of the reason for arrest as required by Article 13(1).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that he was arrested without any reason, was not informed of the reason for his arrest, and that the arrest was unlawful and violated Article 13(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The 1st respondent denied arresting the petitioner and the alleged assault. The 2nd respondent claimed he arrested the petitioner for drunken and disorderly behavior at 9:30 p.m., supported by affidavits from witnesses.
key_facts: Petitioner was arrested at about 6 p.m. on 1 March 1995 without being informed of the reason.
Petitioner was assaulted by the 1st respondent while in custody.
No reasonable grounds or credible information existed for the arrest.
The 1st respondent arrested the petitioner allegedly due to a land dispute involving the 1st respondent's brother-in-law.
The 2nd respondent's version of arrest was rejected by the court as a cover-up.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that Article 13(1) requires that no person be arrested except according to procedure established by law and that the person be informed of the reason for arrest. The arrest must be based on reasonable grounds or credible information.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner was arrested without any grounds or credible information and was not informed of any reason for his arrest. The 1st respondent did not follow the procedure established by law (section 32(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure). Therefore, the arrest violated Article 13(1).
principles_established: Arrest without reasonable grounds or credible information violates Article 13(1).
Failure to inform the arrested person of the reason for arrest breaches Article 13(1).
Procedure established by law includes statutory provisions such as section 32(1)(b) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
precedents_cited: Wijeratne v. Vijitha Perera S.C. App 379/93

outcome.holding: The court declared that the petitioner’s fundamental right under Article 13(1) was violated by the 1st respondent due to unlawful arrest and failure to inform the reason for arrest.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Declaration of violation of Article 13(1) rights; compensation awarded as part of overall relief.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) is central to the court’s reasoning as it defines the legality of the arrest and the requirement to inform the arrested person of the reason, which the court found was breached.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was arrested at about 6 p.m. without being informed of the reason; the 1st respondent arrested him without grounds and did not follow the procedure established by law.
